verdict.tagline: A groundbreaking physics sandbox trapped inside a rough tutorial.
for_you_if: you want deep physics-based combat and sandbox freedom
you love exploring intricate virtual reality environments
you enjoy discovering lore hidden throughout a campaign
not_for_you_if: you struggle with unresponsive controls or technical jank
you expect a polished tutorial right from the start
you have low tolerance for game crashes and performance drops

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players entering the campaign discover deep gunplay and physics systems alongside spaced-out save points.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a campaign alongside arena and sandbox modes.

citations.review_text: Definitely one of the best VR games created during the Index's reign, rivalled only by Half Live: Alyx. The storyline is very well crafted and leaves a lot up to the player to figure out from secrets and hints. The combat is, obviously, fantastic and the ammo as currency system works quite well. Strangely enough, for some reason it says that my brand new gaming PC has a CPU that is "not recommended", but it works fine and looks good. Definitely don't quit Boneworks immediately after completing the story mode, the arenas and, to a lesser extent, the sandboxes, fill about as much playtime combined as the story does.
absolutely insane graphics compared to standalone and beatufiul story mode, arenas, sandbox too. you MUST get it

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game's physics engine allows for interactive grabbing, throwing, climbing, and breaking objects.

citations.review_text:
BONEWORKS is basically what happens when someone gives you a physics engine and says, “Go break everything.”

The physics are easily the best part. Almost everything feels interactive, and there's something incredibly satisfying about grabbing, throwing, climbing, punching, and experimenting with whatever you can find. You can approach situations in surprisingly stupid ways and somehow make them work.

The atmosphere and level design are also great, with plenty of secrets and weird moments to discover. The combat can feel clunky sometimes, but honestly, the jank is part of the charm.

It's not always the smoothest VR experience, and the movement can definitely take some getting used to, but once you get comfortable with it, there's nothing quite like it.

**9/10 — bought a VR game, accidentally became a physics experiment.**

Janky and a bit buggy at times but overall it's a lot of fun and a good way to introduce yourself to VR.

Tutorial is fun and is effective at showing you how to play the game as well as introduce you to the game's story. Gunplay is fun. Moving around and looking at everything is fun. Melee is good. Story is... serviceable. It's kinda just there to push the game along, which is fine, and it doesn't interfere. 

Now maybe it's because it's VR in general, but picking up, moving objects, trying to break objects, and climbing, while fun, can be pretty jank at times. I did get frustrated at times especially trying to climb. The good news is often there are several ways to deal with different parts of the game typically, so you aren't pigeonholed to do things the hard way. 

A significant criticism is that near the end of the game there are just flat out NO save points after a certain point. And I'm wondering if I died, would I have to do ALL THAT WORK over again. Not sure but I'm glad I didn't find out. There might at least have been a checkpoint system at that point, but again, I'd rather not have found out. 

Otherwise yea, very much worth it for a VR game. I played it on a HTC Vive Pro 2 with Valve Index Controllers.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a lack of save points or checkpoints near the end of the campaign.

citations.review_text:
I feel odd negatively reviewing Boneworks. I liked it, and you can have a good time with it. I think the Hammer-esque grid textures and graffiti are a cute aesthetic, the gunplay is fun enough, and the puzzles are stimulating without being overlong.  The physics are robust, and this does have the most consistent and reliable gripping and climbing out of any game I've played with the Index Knuckles' weird capacitive pads. The Ladder proved this to me perfectly, only Boneworks could make that work for me.

However, Boneworks is no longer the gem of VR I assume it was in 2019. Other games have learned what it has to teach, and its innovations are no longer as stunning. Furthermore, my playthrough highlighted for me all the moments it wasn't living up to. Melee combat is limp and inconsistent, with the amount of force required to deal damage (either barehanded or swinging something) feeling near random, and trying to mantle ledges led to a lot of awkward swimming motions at walls trying to get my virtual legs underneath me. This lends an almost insulting air to the "advanced VR users only" disclaimer, with its 'advanced' mechanics coming off as quaint at best. It's also not helped by the barebones and directionless story, difficulty appreciating the sandbox mode due to very stingy unlocks, and a lack of quality of life features I had gotten used to in similar systems (Blade and Sorcery comes to mind). The more I sit with it the more all the little annoyances come to the surface, and I begin to wonder if this was worth the $30 asking price.

It walked so later games could run (almost literally with popularizing joystick movement) but the rough edges show now more than ever, and it is most valuable today as a museum piece, no longer the leading edge. You're buying more of a history lesson in mass-market VR than anything, and you have to be prepared to meet it halfway .

Janky and a bit buggy at times but overall it's a lot of fun and a good way to introduce yourself to VR.

Tutorial is fun and is effective at showing you how to play the game as well as introduce you to the game's story. Gunplay is fun. Moving around and looking at everything is fun. Melee is good. Story is... serviceable. It's kinda just there to push the game along, which is fine, and it doesn't interfere. 

Now maybe it's because it's VR in general, but picking up, moving objects, trying to break objects, and climbing, while fun, can be pretty jank at times. I did get frustrated at times especially trying to climb. The good news is often there are several ways to deal with different parts of the game typically, so you aren't pigeonholed to do things the hard way. 

A significant criticism is that near the end of the game there are just flat out NO save points after a certain point. And I'm wondering if I died, would I have to do ALL THAT WORK over again. Not sure but I'm glad I didn't find out. There might at least have been a checkpoint system at that point, but again, I'd rather not have found out. 

Otherwise yea, very much worth it for a VR game. I played it on a HTC Vive Pro 2 with Valve Index Controllers.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe some levels as dragging on and mention that the climbing mechanics can feel wonky or require getting used to.

citations.review_text: Some of the levels drag on a bit, I especially hate the cardboard boxes everywhere, despite some frustrating moments, I really enjoy the puzzles and the VR pistols and rifles in this game, the smgs are sort of ♥♥♥♥ though.  The climbing is a bit wonky, once you get used to it it's really not a big deal though, you just have to figure it out.  So far I have beaten the main story levels and unlocked a bunch of stuff by thoroughly searching the levels, played some sandbox modes, and some arena modes so a bit of everything.  I especially enjoy the arenas.  I still have a lot to unlock and extra modes to play after beating the story which is awesome.  I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a puzzle shooter style sandbox game that doesn't bog you down with story.  The acting in it was definitely pretty damn corny but it's okay haha, it doesn't happen much and it's not a big deal, you can tell the game really isn't about the story it's about the gameplay.

Enjoyed Bonworks more than Bonelab simply because it got the game.
Actual levels you spend hours exploring. Basic plot that does it's job to set you to go through all of it.
Interactions not always enjoyable for me, but it is what it is.
